title: create aborts a campaign when a member's first command outruns its guest sshd
foundBy: session agent, while running make test-smoke on an unrelated change
details:
`cs-campaign create` aborts a whole campaign when a member's first command reaches its guest before that guest's sshd accepts connections.

`cs-sandbox create` returns once the machine exists and its port forward is up. It does not wait for sshd. `provisionMember` then execs into the guest immediately, and `memberRun` in `internal/cli/sandbox.go` is a bare shell-out with no readiness check and no retry. One refused connection ends the create, after every machine in the fleet has been provisioned.

Which step reports the failure depends on the member's CLI and its auth mode, so the error message moves around. `prepareAuth` returns without any exec for the claude CLI, and for a member authenticating from an inherited login. Those members fail later, in `applyModelConfig`. A member holding an API key execs during `prepareAuth` and fails there instead. Both are the same race.

The orchestrator wins this race every time. It boots against an idle host, while the second member boots beside a machine that is already running and taking host CPU and disk. Every failure observed was on the second member.

These numbers come from `make test-smoke`, which provisions two real machines per scenario. Scenario failures appeared in six of thirteen runs across two commits. Each was preceded by `Connection closed by 127.0.0.1 port <gateway>` and reported as `cs-sandbox exec ...: exit status 255`. One scenario won the race slowly instead of losing it, taking 356 seconds against a usual 59.

The cost is not the retry nobody wrote. A create that fails this way reads as a broken fleet or a bad profile, and the machines are already paid for when it happens.
